sentences.text: Corosaurus was an extinct genus of pistosauroid, a type of marine reptile, found in Wyoming, United States.
The largest known individuals of this animal measured more than 4 meters in length.
Fossils of Corosaurus were found in Jackson Canyon, Wyoming, dating to approximately 247.4 to 245 million years ago.
Ermine Cowles Case named the genus Corosaurus in 1936.
The species name 'alcovensis' refers to the Alcova Limestone Formation where the holotype — the specimen the species is based on — was discovered.
Glenn William Storrs described additional specimens of Corosaurus in 1991.
Oskar Kuhn established the family Corosauridae for Corosaurus in 1961.
The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Corosaurus as Eosauropterygia.
Olivier Rieppel classified Corosaurus as the sister-taxon to a group containing Cymatosaurus, Pistosaurus, and Plesiosauria.
Corosaurus lived during the late Early Triassic period, specifically the late Olenekian stage, between 247.4 and 245 million years ago.
